# crcheck <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />
<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/gigu003/crcheck/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gigu003/crcheck/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

`crcheck` provides tools for checking the validity and internal consistency of
individual tumour records in population-based cancer registry data. It focuses
on common registry variables and clinically meaningful item combinations, using
rule sets derived from IARC/IACR Technical Report No. 42, IARC/IACR multiple
primary rules, ENCR/JRC quality-check resources, and registry field
specifications.

The package is designed for routine cancer registry quality-control workflows:
prepare a case-level data frame, run single-item and multi-item checks, review
the returned issue list, and feed the results back into registry data cleaning.
Core checks use base R where practical; duplicate-person linkage uses
specialized probabilistic and string-comparison dependencies for scale and
reproducibility.

## What can be checked?

| Area | Main functions | Typical variables |
|---|---|---|
| Single-item value ranges | `check_single_item()` | `id`, `sex`, `age`, `topo`, `morp`, `beha`, `grad`, `basi`, `icd10` |
| Date logic | `check_age_birth_inci()`, `check_birth_inci_last()`, `check_followup()` | `birthda`, `inciden`, `deathda`, `lastcontact`, `status` |
| Topography and morphology | `check_topo_morp()` | `topo`, `morp` |
| Age, topography, and morphology | `check_age_topo_morp()` | `age`, `topo`, `morp` |
| Sex, topography, and morphology | `check_sex_topo_morp()` | `sex`, `topo`, `morp` |
| Behaviour, grade, morphology, topography, and basis of diagnosis | `check_beha_topo()`, `check_grad_morp_beha()`, `check_grad_topo_morp_beha()`, `check_basi_morp()` | `beha`, `grad`, `morp`, `topo`, `basi` |
| Possible multiple primary cancers | `check_multiple_primary()` | `id`, `topo`, `morp`, `inciden` |
| Data-frame level quality checks | `cr_check()` | a cancer registry data frame |
| Duplicate-person identification | `check_duplicate_person()` | `id`, `name`, `sex`, `birthda`, optional address and phone |

## Recommended input fields

`cr_check()` works with ordinary data frames. It detects supported variables by
name and matches column names case-insensitively. Commonly used fields include:

```text
id, registr, sex, age, birthda, inciden, topo, morp, beha, grad, basi,
icd10, deathda, lastcontact, status
```

If `age` is absent but both `birthda` and `inciden` are available, `cr_check()`
calculates age internally for age-related consistency checks.

## Installation

You can install the development version of 'crcheck' from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("gigu003/crcheck")
```

## Examples

### Check a single item

Use `check_single_item()` to validate one variable against the package's
value-range rules.

```{r single-item-example}
library(crcheck)

sex <- c("1", "2", "9", "")
res <- check_single_item(sex, var_name = "sex", allow_missing = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
print(res)
```

### Check an item combination

Use item-combination functions when the validity of one variable depends on
another variable. For example, `check_topo_morp()` checks topography and
morphology combinations.

```{r topo-morp-example}
topo <- c("C15.1", "C06.9", "C16.2", "C34.9")
morp <- c(8140, 8500, 8500, 8600)

res <- check_topo_morp(topo, morp, quiet = TRUE)
print(res)
```

### Run comprehensive checks on a data frame

Use `cr_check()` to run available single-item and multi-item checks on a cancer
registry data frame. Column names are matched case-insensitively for supported
variables.

```{r cr-check-example}
df <- data.frame(
  id = c("410102198001011234", "410102198001011235"),
  sex = c(1, 2),
  birthda = c("1980-01-01", "1980-01-01"),
  inciden = c("2020-01-01", "2019-12-31"),
  topo = c("C61.9", "C50.9"),
  morp = c(8140, 8500),
  beha = c(3, 3),
  grad = c(1, 2),
  basi = c(7, 7),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cr_check(df, quiet = TRUE)
```

### Detect possible multiple primary cancers

Use `check_multiple_primary()` when a patient has more than one tumour record.
The function compares tumour pairs within each patient according to the
IARC/IACR 2004 rules for multiple primary cancers.

```{r multiple-primary-example}
mp_data <- data.frame(
  id = c("P1", "P1", "P2", "P2"),
  topo = c("C18.0", "C34.9", "C50.9", "C50.9"),
  morp = c(8140, 8140, 8140, 8070),
  inciden = c("2020-01-01", "2021-03-15", "2019-05-01", "2020-06-01"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

check_multiple_primary(mp_data, inciden = "inciden", quiet = TRUE)
```

### Identify records belonging to the same person

Use `check_duplicate_person()` before checking multiple primaries when a person
may have two, three, or more registry records. It returns strict duplicate
groups together with the pair-level probabilities and field evidence used to
form them.

```{r duplicate-person-example}
person_data <- data.frame(
  record = paste0("R", 1:4),
  id = rep("11010519491231002X", 4),
  name = rep("张三", 4),
  sex = rep(1, 4),
  birthda = rep("1949-12-31", 4),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

duplicates <- check_duplicate_person(
  person_data,
  record_id = "record",
  quiet = TRUE
)
duplicates$groups
duplicates$pairs[, c(
  "row_1",
  "row_2",
  "duplicate_probability",
  "decision"
)]
```

The function does not use transitive chaining: every pair of records within a
group must reach the matching threshold. Probabilities produced without
labelled training data are model estimates conditional on candidate generation
and should be reviewed before records are merged.

### Inspect rule groups

Use `show_rules()` to inspect selected internal rule groups. For example,
`"tomo"` shows topography-morphology rules and `"mult_morp"` shows morphology
groups used by the multiple-primary check.

```{r show-rules-example}
suppressWarnings(head(show_rules("tomo"), 3))
show_rules("mult_morp")[1:3, c("group", "label", "morp")]
```

## Output format

The printed result is a data frame with the following columns:

- `id`: record identifier or row position;
- `item`: checked item or item combination;
- `value`: value that triggered the warning or error;
- `type`: warning or error code;
- `group`: rule group identifier.

In general, `type` values beginning with `E-` indicate errors or invalid values,
whereas values beginning with `W-` indicate warnings or clinically unusual
combinations that should be reviewed. `group` identifies the corresponding
internal rule group; use `show_rules()` to inspect rule definitions where
available.

`check_multiple_primary()` returns a pair-level data frame because possible
multiple primary cancers are assessed by comparing tumour records within the
same patient. Its output includes the patient identifier, row indices, compared
topography and morphology values, mapped rule groups, rule code, and reason.

## Migration to crcheck 0.1.0

Version 0.1.0 consolidates the public API introduced during the package
redesign. Legacy single-item checks now use `check_single_item()`, rule display
helpers now use `show_rules()`, and several combined checks have new interfaces
and result structures. These are intentional breaking changes; legacy function
names are not retained as aliases.

See the [migration guide](vignettes/migration-to-0.1.0.Rmd) for the complete
mapping and the behavior changes that may affect existing workflows.

## Development status and roadmap

The current version keeps the main `cr_check()` output compact for compatibility
with existing workflows. Planned improvements include optional correction
suggestions and more configurable `cr_check()` modules.

## Notes

Internal dictionaries are rebuilt from the maintained generation scripts in
`data-raw/`. Check objects contain only the fields required to represent the
validation result.
